candidates.title: Selmer-converse / exact-BSD chain applied to the rank-0 twist E^{-7} (the only instance in openai/math whose hypotheses the seed satisfies)
candidates.statement: (a) ExactBSD Theorem 1.1 (thm:main), verbatim: 'Let $E/\Q$ be an elliptic curve and let $q$ be any prime. If $s_q(E)\in\{0,1\}$, then $r(E)=a(E)=s_q(E),\ \#\Sha(E/\Q)<\infty$, and, with $r=r(E)$ and the preceding normalizations, $L^{(r)}(E,1)/r! = \Omega_E\Reg_E\,\#\Sha(E/\Q)\prod_{\ell\ finite}c_\ell(E)/\#E(\Q)_{\rm tors}^2$. There are no additional hypotheses on reduction, rational torsion, isogenies, complex multiplication, or residual Galois representations.' Immediately after: 'The rank and finiteness assertions are the unrestricted low-corank converse of [C]; the two-primary leading-term equality is supplied by [B]. ... The new assertion proved here is the exact valuation of the leading-term formula at every odd prime ... The low-Selmer-corank hypothesis is essential to the stated scope.' Normalizations (01-introduction.tex:20-45): Omega_E = integral over ALL real components of the Neron differential; c_ell = [E(Q_ell):E_0(Q_ell)]; L(E,s) with all finite Euler factors. (b) ExactBSD Proposition 10.4 (center:odd-valuations), verbatim: 'For every elliptic curve $E/\Q$ of analytic rank zero or one and every odd prime $p$, $v_p(Q_E)=v_p(\#\Sha(E/\Q))$.' Proof: single-curve inequality (8) X(E)>=0 (Prop 5.11) for E and for the auxiliary twist E^D of Lemma 2.6, plus X(E)+X(E^D)=0 (Cor 10.2, which rests on Thm 9.6 = anticyclotomic main-conjecture equality over the auxiliary K); CM case via Burungale-Flach. (c) ExactBSD Proposition 5.11 (single:center), verbatim: 'The element $U$ of Proposition 5.5 satisfies $X(E)=v_p(U(0))\ge0$. (8) This holds at every odd coefficient prime, for all reduction types and all residual representations of the non-CM curve.' Section 5 standing hypothesis (05-single.tex:3-4): 'E/Q is non-CM and has analytic rank zero or one'; X(E) := v_p(Q_E) - v_p(#Sha(E/Q)). NOTE (checked here): Prop 5.5 invokes Prop 4.2(a) (vertical:tests), and Section 4 opens with 'Use the fields K,F,L and discriminants D,D' of Section 2' and uses 'the disjointness imposed in Section 2' in its residual argument (04-vertical.tex:12-16, 196-198); Lemma 2.6 in turn uses Theorem 2.5 = Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2. So even the rank-0 one-sided bound (c) inherits the Goldfeld2 (and hence Smith 2025 v1) dependency; there is no shorter chain. (d) TwoPrimary Theorem 1.1 (thm:main), verbatim: 'Let $E/\mathbb Q$ be any elliptic curve with $s_2(E)\leq1$. Then $r:=\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{ord}_{s=1}L(E,s)=s_2(E)$, $\#\Sha(E/\mathbb Q)<\infty$. Moreover, $Q_E=L^{(r)}(E,1)(\#T_E)^2/(r!\,\Omega_E\Reg_E\prod_{\ell}c_\ell(E))\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$, $v_2(Q_E)=v_2(\#\Sha(E/\mathbb Q))$. There is no restriction on $E[2]$ or on the reduction of $E$ at two.' (TwoPrimary's height normalization is 2x the usual one; irrelevant in rank 0.) (e) SelmerConverse Theorem 1.1 (thm:main), verbatim: 'For every elliptic curve $A_0/\Q$, every prime $p$, and $r\in\{0,1\}$, $s_p(A_0)=r \Longrightarrow a(A_0)=\rank_{\Z}A_0(\Q)=r, \#\Sha(A_0/\Q)<\infty$. There is no restriction on reduction type, complex multiplication, the residual representation, rational torsion, or rational isogenies.' followed by 'The theorem gives rank equality and finiteness; it does not evaluate the leading coefficient'. Same conclusion claimed by Goldfeld2 Thm 1.1 (p=2, c_2 in {0,1}) and Pointwise2 Thm 1.1 (p=2, E(Q)[2]!=0). WHAT FOLLOWS FOR E^{-7} (rank 0, L(E^{-7},1) != 0 PROVED_COMPUTER_ASSISTED, Sha finite by Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin, so s_q(E^{-7})=0 for every q): (e) adds nothing (its conclusion is the known GZK statement). (a)+(b)+(d) would give, at grade IMPORTED_PREPRINT, #Sha(E^{-7}/Q) = Q_{E^{-7}} := L(E^{-7},1)#E^{-7}(Q)_tors^2/(Omega_{E^{-7}} prod_ell c_ell(E^{-7})) exactly, i.e. v_p #Sha(E^{-7})[p^inf] = v_p(Q_{E^{-7}}) at p = 2 (via (d)), at p = 3, 7, 2243, 4547, 5843 (bad for E^{-7}: split mult. at 3 and 5843, nonsplit at 2243, type III at 4547, I0* at 7, I1* at 2) and at every good p, with no residual-image hypothesis. (c) alone gives only the upper bound v_p #Sha(E^{-7})[p^inf] <= v_p(Q_{E^{-7}}) at odd p. HOW IT FEEDS THE SEED: (i) K-route: the lab's frozen route (reference/07_good_primes.tex:67) reads: '...derived-height theory of Bertolini-Darmon then gives Div Sha(E/K)[p^inf]=0 with the exponent bound v_p#Sha(E/K)[p^inf] <= 2c, where p^c is the exponent of B=Sha(E^{-7}/Q)[p^inf]. Because Sha(E/K)[p^inf] = Sha(E/Q)[p^inf] + B for odd p, and the Cassels-Tate pairing on the finite group B forces #B >= p^{2c}, the summand Sha(E/Q)[p^inf] vanishes.' This conclusion holds for EVERY value of c; the exact c from ExactBSD is NOT an input. The route's live hypotheses are a unit c_2(p) (M_2(p) != 0, 'open at every prime', 07_good_primes.tex:77) and BLV equality at ordinary p; neither is touched by any openai/math result. Net gain for (i): none. (ii) Plectic route at 5843: FG Thm 3.4 + corank Sel_{5843^inf}(E^{-7})=0 (already known by GZK) gives Sha(E/Q)[5843^inf] finite; the only NEW content would be the exact order of Sha(E^{-7}/Q)[5843^inf] (= v_5843(Q_{E^{-7}})), which does not enter lemma TH, the converse of FG Thm 3.4, or the order of Sha(E/Q)[5843^inf]. Net gain for (ii): none for E. (iii) Q36: L(E/K,s)=L(E,s)L(E^{-7},s) and BSD(E/K) <=> BSD(E/Q) and BSD(E^{-7}/Q) by Milne restriction of scalars + Cassels-Tate isogeny invariance (ExactBSD Prop 2.4, 02-classical.tex:72-96, itself published Milne 1972 / Cassels 1965; Sha(E/K)[p^inf] = Sha(E)[p^inf] + Sha(E^{-7})[p^inf] for odd p). Exact BSD for E^{-7} therefore makes the K-level rank-2 leading-term identity EQUIVALENT to Q36 over Q (modulo 2-power/period bookkeeping) but supplies no rank-2 archimedean (Gross-Zagier-type) comparison; every manuscript disclaims the leading term in rank >= 2 (ExactBSD 01-introduction.tex:67; TwoPrimary 01-introduction.tex:18-20; Pointwise2 introduction.tex:35-37). Net gain for (iii): bookkeeping only.

candidates.title: Lab-side prerequisites flagged by the maps: correct the twist's conductor record, compute the BSD quotient Q_{E^{-7}} exactly, and pin Sha(E^{-7})[2^inf] unconditionally by 2-descent
candidates.statement: (a) MeanRank Lemma 2.2 (setup:local-factors), verbatim: 'For $F\in\mathcal F$ and admissible $d$, $L_{F^{(d)}}(s)=\sum_{n\ge1}\lambda_F(n)\chi_d(n)n^{-s}$, $q_{F^{(d)}}=q_F|d|^2$' (admissible: d = 1 mod 4, (d, Q_S)=1; d=-7 is admissible for the seed). Hence the conductor of E^{-7} is 49N, NOT N as SEED_CONTEXT.md line 36 records ('conductor N, same bad primes'): 7 does not divide N, the twist by Q(sqrt-7) is ramified exactly at 7, so E^{-7} has additive reduction of type I_0^* at 7. Derived here from the recorded seed data (to be verified by Tate's algorithm, not taken from any manuscript): -7 = 1 mod 8 so E^{-7} = E over Q_2 (I1*, c_2=2 unchanged); chi_{-7}(3)=chi_{-7}(2243)=chi_{-7}(5843)=-1 (inert) so 3: I2 split (c=2), 2243: I1 nonsplit (c=1), 5843: I2 split (c=2); chi_{-7}(4547)=+1 so type III unchanged (c=2); at 7: I_0^* with c_7 in {2,4} since E^{-7}(Q)[2] != 0. (b) Goldfeld2 Lemma 13.5 proof (03-heegner.tex:723-736): 'a ramified quadratic twist of good reduction at an odd prime q has type I_0^* and component number #E[2]^{Fr_q}' (citing Barrios et al. 2025 Thm 4.1; classical) - gives c_7(E^{-7}) = #E[2](F_7)-type count. (c) Goldfeld2 Lemma 2.4 (pr:finite-descent), verbatim: 'Let $F$ be the quotient of $\Sha(E/\Q)[2^\infty]$ by its maximal divisible subgroup. Then $d_2(E)=c_2(E)+\dim_{\F_2}F[2]$, and $\dim_{\F_2}F[2]$ is even.' (classical: alternating Cassels-Tate pairing). For E^{-7}: Sha finite by GZK, c_2=0, so dim Sha(E^{-7})[2] = dim Sel_2(E^{-7}) - dim E^{-7}(Q)[2], computable by a 2-isogeny/2-descent (E^{-7} has the rational 2-torsion point (0,0)); if that difference is 0, Sha(E^{-7})[2^inf]=0 unconditionally. (d) Needed to make twist-E-7 testable at all: Q_{E^{-7}} = L(E^{-7},1) #E^{-7}(Q)_tors^2 / (Omega_{E^{-7}} prod_ell c_ell(E^{-7})) with Omega over both real components (ExactBSD/TwoPrimary normalization); L(E^{-7},1) in [9.054319, 9.054421] must be sharpened until the rational Q_{E^{-7}} (denominator bounded by #tors^2) is pinned, then v_p(Q_{E^{-7}}) read off at p = 2, 3, 7, 2243, 4547, 5843 and small good p. The BSD-predicted #Sha(E^{-7}) is the quantity ExactBSD claims to certify.

candidates.statement: Dependency DAG (sweep-deps, no cycle): Goldfeld2 (root; imports Smith, 'The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture implies Goldfeld's conjecture', arXiv:2503.17619 v1, Theorem 1.1, an unrefereed human preprint, for its Thm 1.2) -> SelmerConverse (p=2 case and auxiliary fields: 02-reduction.tex:36-61 'We use the following two established results ... These are [Goldfeld2, Theorems 1.1 and 1.2]') -> TwoPrimary (main Thm 1.1 cites no OAI paper in its proof; Cor 1.2/16.1 import SelmerConverse/Goldfeld2) -> ExactBSD (imports [C]=SelmerConverse Thm 1.1 and 37 internal lemmas, [B]=TwoPrimary Thm 1.1 and 18 internal lemmas 'with p in place of two', Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2; 57 OAI citation sites in oai_cites_raw.json). Red flags recorded by the maps: (1) all determinant identities rest on 'matrix limits on a fixed nonprincipal ultrafilter' of finite Artin-ring cochain models (ExactBSD Lemma 3.1, 03-models.tex:47-115; TwoPrimary Lemma 3.1, 03-foundations.tex:223-256; SelmerConverse 'admissible cochains' Def 3.4, 03-tame-deformation.tex:239) - non-constructive, no published antecedent; (2) Kato 2004 Thm 9.5/12.5(3) invoked at p=2 (TwoPrimary 04-siegel.tex:258-265; Goldfeld2 04-cyclotomic.tex:245-260, which concedes the comparison scalar 'need not have a uniformly bounded 2-valuation'); (3) ExactBSD's October-3 edition cited '\cite{B,C,Dv}' with Dv a dangling key to 'a removed supporting manuscript' (history.md Oct-7 fix; 01-introduction.tex:134), whose content is unrecoverable; (4) extraordinary scope: anticyclotomic main-conjecture EQUALITY (Thm 9.6), mu=0 (Prop 6.5, resting on Chai 2003 unpublished), Kato-type divisibility at every odd p including p=3, p | N and reducible residual representations, while stating Skinner-Urban/JSW are 'not used here' (ExactBSD 01-introduction.tex:98-111); (5) SelmerConverse's load-bearing U(3,1) theta/cusp-lifting/Galois chain (Sections 4-9) and its p | N extension of BDP (05-constant-terms.tex:224-337) are asserted in a few sentences; its appendix on the nonstandard weighted fundamental lemma cites an undated 185-page author draft and is never used; (6) no Lean artifact for family 002 or 006 (sweep-lean: lean/docs has no 002.md/006.md; formalization.yaml has no entry; review status of the whole catalogue 'unchecked'); (7) the Sept/Oct revisions changed only dates and citation pointers (diff -r), so no proof-repair round has touched this family. Grade cap: IMPORTED_PREPRINT (K-GRADE).

candidates.statement: Statements found: (1) ExactBSD Prop 5.5 (single:integral), verbatim: 'The generic cohomology of $G$ is a line in degree one, and $z$ is nonzero on that line. If $U_0\in\Frac R$ is its coordinate in the inverse determinant relative to an integral generator, then $U=(U_0/\Delta)\prod_{q\in S_f\setminus\{p\}}D_q/P_q\in R\setminus\{0\}$ (3)' - a Kato-zeta-element-in-the-determinant (one-sided cyclotomic IMC) statement over Z_p[[t,u_1..u_k]] at every odd p, all reduction types, all residual representations, for NON-CM E of ANALYTIC RANK <= 1 (05-single.tex:3-4 standing hypothesis), and depending on Prop 4.2 (auxiliary fields of Lemma 2.6). (2) ExactBSD Prop 5.11 (quoted in twist-E-7): X(E) >= 0 at every odd p under the same rank <= 1 hypothesis. (3) ExactBSD Prop 6.1 (pair:primitive): BDP/Coleman primitive 'imposes no ordinary-reduction hypothesis on the target E', p | N allowed (06-pair.tex:84-106); Prop 6.5: 'p does not divide B_w (14)' = mu=0 for the BDP-type measure, p SPLIT in K (06-pair.tex:406-413); Cor 6.9 / Thm 9.6 (unit:unit-comparison): 'The two quotients $U_w$ are units' = anticyclotomic main-conjecture equality at every odd p, p split in auxiliary K, all bad primes split in K, rank E(K)=1 (09-unit.tex:396-449). (4) TwoPrimary Prop 5.1 / Lemma 5.7 (2-adic Kato class in the determinant lattice, non-CM; 'if an(A_0)=0, then v_2 U(0)=X(A_0)', 05-positive-determinant.tex:34-61, 501-555) and Lemma 7.5 (nonzero Selmer Bockstein, corank-one, 07-positive-completion.tex:237-346). (5) Goldfeld2 Lemma 12.4 (residual freeness of the 2-adic cyclotomic complex for reducible E[2], 04-cyclotomic.tex:580-659). (6) SelmerConverse eq. (5.katz-abelian-log): BDP-type inverse-theta primitive and abelian logarithm extended to p | N ('No ordinary hypothesis on A_0 at p has entered'), p split in auxiliary K (05-constant-terms.tex:224-337); Lemma 3.6 uniform local logarithm estimate 'including at bad reduction' (03-tame-deformation.tex:688-733). Hypothesis check for E at 2243 (I1 split), 4547 (type III, pot. supersingular), 5843 (I2 nonsplit), 3 (I2 nonsplit), 2 (I1*): every one of (1)-(6) requires analytic rank <= 1, Selmer corank <= 1, or rank E(K)=1 over an auxiliary K in which all bad primes split; the seed has a(E) >= 2, s_p(E) >= 2 for all p, rank E(K)=2 for every K, and in the lab's K = Q(sqrt-7) the primes 3, 2243, 5843 are inert. No statement in the repository is an IMC, control theorem, or Euler-system divisibility for a curve of Selmer corank 2 at any prime. Therefore nothing can replace any hypothesis of the lab's S.3-type chain (IMC + control + height nondegeneracy + leading term) or of B.18 at 2243, 4547, 5843, nor Sprung/Kobayashi-type signed theory at good supersingular p (23, 29, 131, ...). For E^{-7} (rank 0) items (1)-(2) are the ingredients of twist-E-7 and are not separately useful. Published comparison: Kato 2004 Sec. 17 (good p, large image) and Skinner 2016 (nonsplit multiplicative) already cover E^{-7} at good primes with large image and at 3; the manuscripts' only would-be novelty for E^{-7} is at 2243, 4547, 5843, 7 and at good primes with unrecorded image - all unusable until the chain is graded.

candidates.why_promising: Mandatory topic; negative. The repository's anticyclotomic results live entirely in the indefinite, split-prime, rank-one Heegner world; the lab's obstacle is definite, inert, exceptional-zero, rank two. The only conceptual overlap (Kolyvagin-derivative finite/singular switch at inert auxiliary primes, TwoPrimary Prop 9.7 / Goldfeld2 Lemma 13.12) is 2-adic and for a Heegner K, hence not transferable to the level-raised theta element at 5843.

candidates.title: Any conclusion valid for Selmer corank 2 or analytic rank 2 (expected none) - confirmed none, with locations
candidates.statement: Exhaustive list of statements that mention rank >= 2 in any form: (1) Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2 (thm:main-density): 'For every elliptic curve E/Q and each j in {0,1}, lim #{d in D(X): a(E^{(d)})=j}/#D(X) = 1/2 ... Consequently the twists of analytic rank at least two have density zero.' - a density-zero statement about the family; the seed E = E^{(1)} lies in that density-zero set and nothing pointwise is asserted. (2) MeanRank Thm 1.2 (thm:tail): 'there are constants C_E > 0 and an integer R_E >= 1 such that, for every integer R >= R_E, limsup_{Y->inf} (1/Y) sum_{d in D(Y), a(E^{(d)})>R} a(E^{(d)}) <= C_E/R' with R_E >= 65536 forced (model.tex:263-265); Lemma 6.2: 'a(F^{(d)}) <<_E log(3X)' (Jensen); Lemma 4.1: the exact Mellin identity (1+epsilon_d(-1)^k) S_d = ell^{-k} g_d^{(k)}(0), which at k=2, d=1 is the standard smoothed formula for Lambda''(E,1) already used numerically by the lab. (3) Explicit disclaimers: ExactBSD 01-introduction.tex:64-70 'The low-Selmer-corank hypothesis is essential to the stated scope: it is not replaced here by a hypothesis on Mordell-Weil rank alone'; TwoPrimary 01-introduction.tex:18-20 'it makes no assertion about higher Selmer corank or the remaining prime parts'; Pointwise2 introduction.tex:35-37 'It does not assert the full Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer leading-coefficient formula'; SelmerConverse 01-introduction.tex:42-44 'it does not evaluate the leading coefficient'; Goldfeld2 00-introduction.tex:90-91. (4) No derived-height, second-derivative, p-adic-BSD-in-rank-2, plectic, or rank-2 Gross-Zagier statement exists anywhere in the 719 manuscripts (sweep-overview negative results (1); sweep-lean: no Selmer/Sha/L-function-of-E object formalized). The parity statements (Goldfeld2 Lemma 2.2, TwoPrimary Lemma 2.1, SelmerConverse eq. root-sign via Dokchitser-Dokchitser 2010 Thm 1.4) are consistent with s_p(E) = 2 even and w(E) = +1 but are published and add nothing.

candidates.title: Explicit constructions (2-Selmer matrices, Brandt/supersingular-set theta lifts, modular-symbol/theta-element coefficients) that might cheapen Kurihara witnesses, B.18 production symbols, M_2(p) or c_1(lambda_ell)
candidates.statement: Constructions found: (1) Pointwise2 Lemma 7.3 (co:theta-bridge): 'the reduced modular parametrization followed by lambda_M admits an integral weighted ternary theta lift ... a classical holomorphic weight-3/2 form g_M ... of level supported on S cup {l} ... a_M(D) = c_0 2^{omega(N)} zeta_M(D) lambda_M(red_l(L P_D)) (mod 2^M)', built on 'B the definite quaternion algebra ramified at l and infinity, R an Eichler order of level N, supersingular set X = B^x \ B-hat^x / R-hat^x' (coefficients.tex:256-532); Prop 7.4 (co:odd) and Goldfeld2 Prop 4.2 (05-coefficients.tex:270-658, key identity (4.14)) are the same construction, 2-adic, with l = -1 mod 2^M inert in the genus fields and the Heegner hypothesis on K. Cost: enumeration of the supersingular set at level N*l, i.e. class number ~ N l/12 prod(1+1/p) - STRICTLY LARGER than the seed-scale definite Shimura set (~5e14 classes, TASK.md/07_good_primes.tex:77) already judged unaffordable; the weights need 2^M-division points of Heegner points. (2) Pointwise2 Prop 7.1 / Goldfeld2 Prop 4.1 (even coefficient system, Waldspurger: '2v(a(D)/a(D_0)) = v(L_*(sigma D)/L_*(sigma D_0))'): weight-3/2 forms of level ~4N with N = 6.5e15 - infeasible and 2-adic only. (3) Goldfeld2 Prop 8.2 (selmer-matrix-bound: 'dim_{F_2} Sel_2(E^{(h)}/Q) >= sum_i dim ker M_i - C', irreducible E[2]) and H10Q Lemma 3.4 (par:descent: 'dim_{F_2} Sel_2(E_l/Q) = 3' for y^2 = x(x-l)(x+3l) via Monsky/Redei matrices): 2-Selmer lower bounds / specific families, not applicable (seed E[2] reducible with E(Q)[2] = Z/2, not in that family). (4) ExactBSD Prop 5.2/5.4 (Kato Siegel-unit classes, norm relations '1 - a_l(f)[l]/l + [l]^2/l', explicit reciprocity '+- Delta_nu L^{(M)}(f,nu,1)/Omega_0 delta_xi(a)'): re-normalized published Kato, no algorithm; Prop 6.1 (ordinary primitive, measure mu on Z_p^x): BDP-type, needs p split in K. (5) SelmerConverse: 'no algorithmic/computational statement' (map notes); its Lemma 4.1/Prop 4.3 theta forms are on U(3,1) over a real quadratic F. (6) Nonvanishing existence: Pointwise2 Prop 6.1/6.2, Goldfeld2 Prop 3.8, SelmerConverse Lemma 2.3 - existence only, no explicit d; published theorems (Murty-Murty 1991, BFH 1990, Ono-Skinner 1998, Waldspurger) already give this. (7) Repository-wide (sweep-overview): family 142 deterministic F_p factorization in O(((n+1)log p)^{10^12}) bit operations; 107 omega <= 9/4; 109 integer multiplication O(n (lg n)^{1-2^{-182}}); 130 DFT O(n (log n)^{1-10^{-13}}) - all galactic. (8) Lean: the only elliptic-curve code is an uncatalogued 2-descent on y^2 = x^3 - 25x (OAI/NumberTheory/SingleFold/{DescentMap,Rank,Torsion}.lean), a pattern only. Verdict per lab computation: Kurihara witnesses at good p (Mazur-Tate elements) - nothing; B.18 production symbols [a/l]^+ at 2243/4547/5843 (31.6k-74k core-hours) - nothing; Gross-packet second moment M_2(p) on the definite Shimura set (ramified {3,2243,5843,inf}, level 2^3 4547^2) - the only related construction is the SAME kind of definite-quaternion enumeration at larger level; lemma TH coefficient c_1(lambda_ell) of the level-raised theta element at 5843 - nothing (no level-raising at an odd inert prime anywhere).

candidates.why_promising: Mandatory topic; negative. The Brandt/supersingular-set theta constructions are the closest relatives of the lab's Gross-packet computation but run at level N*l on the same kind of class set the lab cannot enumerate, and are 2-adic with a Heegner-hypothesis K; nothing offers a spectral projector or a cheaper evaluation of M_2(p).

Pointwise2 Lemma 4.5, Prop 4.6, Cor 4.1, Lemma 5.9, Prop 7.9/Thm 8.3 (and Goldfeld2 Lemma 13.2, Prop 13.3, Lemma 13.5 (except the Tamagawa fact used in e7-local-data), Lemmas 13.13/13.14, Lemmas 11.4/11.5, Thm 5.10, Thm 6.6, Prop 4.4, Prop 7.7, Lemma 14.1): 2-adic local-condition bookkeeping, ring-class characters, prime-graph combinatorics and uniformity lemmas internal to the 2-converse; none has seed content.

Alternative Heegner field for the plectic route (Pointwise2 Prop 6.1/6.2, Goldfeld2 Prop 3.8, SelmerConverse Lemma 2.3 existence of twists with prescribed local splitting): published theorems already give existence at better grade, and rank E(K') >= 2 for every imaginary quadratic K' kills every rank-<=1 Heegner/BDP route regardless of K'.

Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2 (Goldfeld density) and Cor 1.3 (finite Selmer criterion d_2 in {0,1}): density statement is silent on d=1 and d=-7 pointwise; Cor 1.3 for E^{-7} reduces to the classical Lemma 2.4 + GZK (kept inside e7-local-data-and-2-descent); for E, d_2(E)=2 fails.

MeanRank Thm 1.1 (mean analytic rank 1/2, conditional on Goldfeld2 Thm 1.2), Cor 1.3 (rank moments, conditional on Koymans-Smith arXiv:2606.31649v1), Lemma 2.1, Props 3.1-3.7, Prop 4.4, Lemma 5.2, Props 5.3/5.6/5.9, Prop 6.1: statistical statements over dyadic twist families with ineffective thresholds (R_E >= 65536); nothing pointwise about E or E^{-7}. (Lemma 2.2 kept in e7-local-data; Thm 1.2/Lemmas 4.1, 6.2 recorded under rank-2-anything.)

Fontaine-Mazur modularity at the prime 2 (Thm 1.1, Thm 7.1, Thm 5.1, Props 3.1-8.7): 2-adic Galois-representation modularity only; E and E^{-7} are modular by BCDT at a higher grade; no Selmer/Sha/L-value/Iwasawa content; load-bearing unverifiable import Thorne arXiv:2608.07186v1 Thm D.

Hilbert's tenth problem over Q (Thm 1.1, Cor 7.1, Props 2.2/2.3/2.9, Thm 2.4, Lemmas 3.5, 6.1-6.3): logic/definability paper; its only elliptic-curve theorems are imported 2-converses (corank<=1) and a 2-Selmer computation for y^2=x(x-l)(x+3l) with full 2-torsion (seed has E(Q)_tors = Z/2).

Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields (Thm 1.1 and all of Sections 3-9): conclusion for E/Q(sqrt-7) is classical (BCDT + cyclic base change + Carayol/Saito); no L-value, Selmer, Sha, height or Iwasawa statement; rests on Caraiani-Newton arXiv:2301.10509v3 used outside its stated hypotheses.
